title: MIT OpenCourseWare — Projection Matrices and Least Squares
use: Further study of orthogonal projections and least-squares geometry. The library uses original examples and problems.
verification: Official session page and corresponding lecture-summary PDF retrieved; method/further-study route, not independent manuscript certification

title: Eugene F. Fama and Kenneth R. French — The Capital Asset Pricing Model: Theory and Evidence (2004)
use: Primary author paper on the market portfolio/proxy problem, regression pricing restrictions, hypothesis interpretation and implementation limits. The chapter treats the paper's empirical assessment as dated 2004, not current market evidence.
verification: Actual 22-page Dartmouth-hosted PDF inspected: printed pp.25–26 scope/common beliefs; pp.29–34 risk-free assumptions, beta and zero-intercept tests, imprecise estimated betas and proxy-efficiency interpretation; pp.40–42 market-proxy, nontraded-wealth and rationality/model ambiguity. Publication Journal of Economic Perspectives 18(3), 25–46. No historical dataset, source portfolio, result magnitude or figure reproduced. Original counterexamples and pedagogical sample are independently constructed.

title: Andrew W. Lo, MIT 15.401 — Lectures 15–17: The CAPM and APT (Fall 2008), scoped APT discussion
use: Primary teaching route for multiple systematic factors, linear pricing restrictions and the need to specify factors; this chapter supplies its own finite-state exact-spanning proof and a separate conditional diversification bound.
verification: Reached the actual 29-page official PDF through the MIT course page and read extracted text on slides 15–17 (physical pages 15–17) covering APT, factor choice and regression implementation. Image-only equations were not claimed as extracted text. The source summary is not treated as a proof of exact pricing with residual risk or a uniform asymptotic theorem; those limits are stated and independently derived here. Historical portfolios, empirical magnitudes, graphs and source exercises are not reused.

title: Kenneth R. French Data Library — Description of Fama/French Factors, scoped construction definitions
use: Primary factor-provider illustration of a traded market excess-return series, long-minus-short portfolio spreads, stated size/book-equity inputs and calendar construction. No downloaded performance observations or evidence of a future premium are used.
verification: Read the actual official HTML construction section (retrieved lines 21–40): six underlying value-weight portfolios, SMB/HML spread definitions, market minus safe return and prior-year/book-equity and June/December market-equity information. The chapter cites the method documentation as an example of an explicit rule and vintage requirement. It does not reproduce factor data, claim research returns equal implementable net returns, endorse current performance or adopt the changing safe-rate provider series.
